Pakistan says it killed 28 militants, Afghan Taliban and UN report three civilian deaths KABUL/ISLAMABAD, Sept 21 (Reuters) - Pakistan's government said on Monday that it launched airstrikes in the Afghanistan-Pakistan border region, killing at least 28 militants, with one security official saying two Afghan provinces were targeted.Hours earlier, Afghan Taliban officials accused Islamabad of killing at least three civilians in overnight airstrikes on Afghan territory.The UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) confirmed the deaths of three civilians: a man, a woman and a girl.The attacks broke nearly three months of relative calm. Security forces kill 37 terrorists in KP operations, air strikes: govt Security forces killed 37 terrorists in intelligence-based ground operations in Kohat and Hangu and subsequent precision air strikes targeting terrorist hideouts in the border region with Afghanistan, the Ministry of Information said on Monday.In a post on X, the ministry said the operations were launched following multiple recent terrorist attacks against civilians in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.According to the ministry, security forces conducted an intelligence-based ground operation against a group of terrorists in Kohat and Hangu districts on September 20, killing nine terrorists belonging to “Indian proxy Fitna Al-Khwarij”.
